corpusSummary: This corpus of 2026 social-science work on large language models reveals a field intensifying scrutiny of AI’s social effects, epistemic roles, and governance. Across health, education, policy, and everyday life, researchers examine AI’s trust dynamics, anthropomorphism, and risk management; harness LLMs as methodological tools; investigate AI-enabled learning and counseling; and analyze AI’s influence on organizations, climate, and public discourse. Common threads emphasize transparency, ethics, literacy, and robust evaluation.

themes.name: Trust, embodiment, and social perception of AI
themes.description: Studies cluster around how AI appears to users—humanness, empathy, social presence—and how these cues shape trust, attachment, and behavior, including potential dependency and misalignment with human experience.

themes.name: AI as methodological tool and governance
themes.description: A growing strand documents how LLMs can augment qualitative and quantitative research, from public opinion surveys to ethics-review automation, while highlighting validity, transparency, and governance challenges.

themes.name: AI in education and literacy
themes.description: Research explores AI-enabled tutoring, assessment, design education, AI literacy for diverse groups, and the implications for pedagogy and equity.

themes.name: AI in health, misinformation, and wellbeing
themes.description: A substantial portion examines AI’s role in health information, patient education, misinformation, and governance to protect wellbeing and equity.
